entry.title: In defense of bad coffee
entry.content:
Coffee is one of the wonderful indulgences of life. I don’t think it’s hard to see that I deeply appreciate taking something raw and unrefined and seeking to perfect it. I often find however that I encounter cups of coffee I do not enjoy precisely at those shops that others rave about. I think that the simple explanation is that taste and the “goodness” of things is subjective. However, I believe this to be a far more interesting question than what that reading gives it credit for.

Greatness as a concept fascinates me, often precisely because it is so often conflated with goodness. Let us define some terms. First by goodness I mean simply how much something is enjoyed. I think a good illustration of this concept is how when Michelin-starred chefs are asked about the best meal they’ve ever had, they often refer to their mother’s or grandmother’s cooking. I hope we can agree that both of these food experiences are very good. However, they are without question distinct. Let us call the axis that defines that distinction “Zorp”. Zorp is orthogonal to goodness, but is not itself “greatness”.

What then is greatness?

I think this is the interesting question. Here I do not mean interesting to mean correct, but rather precisely incorrect. I think it is an inherently unknowable truth, and that is exactly what makes it so exciting.

Recently, I’ve been listening to a lot of guitar. It is clear that the playing of popular artists like Santana, Prince, and Jimi Hendrix are all distinct but occupy a similar echelon in terms of greatness. I believe this illustrates the pursuit of greatness to be a fundamentally noble pursuit despite its inherent folly. We must allow people to ponder the unanswerable.

So it is with music and so it is with coffee. We must allow this pursuit of greatness in flavor even if it is folly or we do not appreciate its results.

However, I believe an equally dangerous pitfall to be to lose our appreciation for things that don’t seek to maximize some quality. Is a hilarious comedy any less than a nuanced drama? Is that same comedy any less than the simple joys of a child’s imagination? I think not. We must as a society simultaneously appreciate these seemingly diametrically opposed concepts.

Accepting this at a societal level is in no way sufficient. We must also accept this at an individual level. I believe this to be one of my more significant flaws. I like what I like and often find it difficult to understand or empathize with the viewpoints of others in appreciating what it is that brings them joy. However, I have often found that it is only by opening myself up to these experiences that run counter-parallel to my traditional enjoyment that I am able to live my most fulfilled life.

Who am I to say what makes a cup of coffee good or bad? It is only by opening ourselves up to disappointment that we may learn. Only by setting aside our own biases that we may grow.

And for that, I am grateful for bad coffee—for every cup of coffee I have ever enjoyed was once a cup I gulped down and detested.
entry.summary: Goodness, greatness, and staying open to cups we do not enjoy.

entry.title: A new style of blog post

link.title: A new style of blog post

entry.content:
I recently sought to bring life to this blog. Unfortunately, I found that I too easily fell into the trap of over-editing, to the point that my posts lost my voice.

And so, I have made the radical decision to write my posts by hand. I recently got a new fountain pen, and I have found writing cursive with it on nice paper to have brought back an enjoyment of writing in me that I had long since thought forgotten.

Enjoy these unadulterated windows into my mind.
entry.summary: Handwritten posts, a fountain pen, and writing without over-editing.

entry.title: On passion
entry.content:
I’ve spent much of my free time this past week at a paper store learning about paper. What a joy it must be to run a store for something you love so much.

I hope for a similar thing for my future. I’ve always loved people who genuinely love their work. Perhaps that is why I ended up at a school with the motto “my heart is in the work!” Despite all the criticism that statement gets, I do find it to be a beautiful notion.

What a joy it is to be utterly and irrevocably in love with your work and how lucky I am to be able to feel such a joy.
entry.summary: A paper store, a school motto, and being in love with your work.

entry.title: On knowledge
entry.content:
I have always loved learning. If I had to summarize what I am most passionate about in one word, that word would be learning.

Today I walked out of a meeting for my lab and walked out smiling with the wonder of a child. My labmates all asked such interesting questions. It made me feel so joyous to be surrounded by so many people who were so intelligent, but greater than that, so curious. I feel so lucky to be able to learn from such people.

I have for a while now been mulling over my future, and I think the biggest question was built around the PhD. I believe I have been approaching this question entirely incorrectly. A PhD is a doctorate in philosophy. I take philosophy here to mean a curiosity of all that is around and within us. It is so incredible that I have this opportunity to spend 6 years being curious about the world around me. Obviously, it doesn’t stop there. It seems to me that a scientist’s job is put simply to be curious about the world around them.

What an exciting life!
entry.summary: Curiosity, the company of the curious, and what a PhD actually is.

entry.title: On leisure
entry.content:
Aristotle believed leisure to be the ultimate goal of human life. To our modern sensibilities this may seem odd. I believe here it is important to perhaps think deeper.

The word school traces its origins to the Greek word scholē. Scholē translating to leisure. I quite appreciate this framing. It requires a certain level of freedom to pursue an education and we who have received one are so lucky to have been able to do so.

I do appreciate seeing the implications of this idea. It is unfortunate, but many of history’s examples of leisure are often built upon the oppression of others. However, I don’t believe this to be a necessary condition. Assuming this is true, we can begin to stumble onto such an exciting world of possibilities.

I believe we can enter a world where with those with the soul of an artist would be fully freed to practice their art, those with the soul of an artisan their craft, and those with the soul of a scientist their science.

I believe this to be a fascinating possibility to which we must remain open.
entry.summary: Scholē, education, and a world where artists, craftsmen, and scientists are free to practice.
